tasks.short: Describe and demonstrate products for viewers

steps.what: Read the product brief, purchase details and permitted claims
Practise handling the actual product and choose a truthful demonstration
Write the product description and demonstration cue notes

loop.purpose: Draft concise spoken wording from supplied product facts and the actual demonstration
loop.input: checked product brief, offer details and announcer's demonstration decisions
loop.output: draft product description and cue notes
loop.check: Announcer checks each claim, qualification, price and purchase instruction against the brief and removes any invented benefit or demonstration result
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unclear offers return to manual wording
loop.why_not_simpler: Conversational product wording must fit the particular demonstration and available airtime

steps.what: Check the final cue notes against the product and current offer
Describe or demonstrate products and explain where viewers may purchase them

tasks.design: Use native product-brief links and an existing cue format in {DOCS}, with a bounded draft of the actual product description. The announcer handles the product, chooses the demonstration, checks the final cues and delivers the presentation personally; no synthetic voice, automated broadcast or trailing presentation log is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spoken product wording and cue notes must be assembled from product and offer information.
tasks.enabler_now: Native brief links can reduce searching, and bounded wording assistance can express checked facts in the show format.
tasks.still_hard: Truthful demonstrations, changing offers and responding appropriately when the product behaves unexpectedly.
tasks.human_edge: Showing how the actual product works without overstating what viewers should expect.
tasks.altitude: Less cue preparation, with unchanged live presentation and claim responsibility.

reach.task: Check whether a demonstration fits the show's timing and product brief
reach.learn: Programme format and evidence supporting commercial claims

evidence.claim: LanguageTool offers Dutch spelling, grammar and rephrasing assistance; this establishes wording-tool availability, not truthfulness of product claims.
Source-linked cue drafting, native brief lookup and all task-specific retained-time estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary includes product research, physical demonstration preparation, the real cue-note write, final checking and public delivery. It does not hide cue writing inside live performance. If the announcer receives finished cues and writes none, that authorship work belongs to its actual producer and no focal writing benefit is claimed.

The commercial team supplies product ID, feature evidence, allowed claims, price, currency, purchase channel, offer conditions and validity time in the existing brief. s1 counts source and current-version checking, retaining 17 hours. Missing or expired offer information requires manual clarification rather than inferred availability.

The announcer produces demonstration choices in s2 and captures the selected facts, wording and timing in s3's retained 9 hours. s4 retains all final claim, qualification and purchase-instruction checks. No structured sold-out flag, product-success claim or automatic offer update is assumed.

Test native brief links and cue templates before custom code. Ordinary cue saves have no approval stage or saving; the gate covers the exact final cues used in the external presentation, and changed live conditions require fresh human judgement.
unknowns: Who currently authors product cue notes
Frequency of offer changes and actual cue-preparation time
research_questions: Does bounded cue drafting reduce total writing and correction effort without introducing unsupported product claims?

already_counted.description: Verify product sources, correct cue wording and check the final presentation content

incremental.description: Maintain brief and cue links and sample unsupported commercial wording

approvals.approved_version: Exact final cue version, product, demonstration, offer conditions and purchase instructions checked in s4; changes invalidate approval and unexpected live conditions require the announcer's fresh judgement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=91, gross=9, upkeep=1, net=8. Cautious case: a changing offer retains all 20 source hours and a tightly constrained demonstration retains 14 of 15 cue-writing hours; other 65 hours stay, giving 1 gross minus 1 upkeep =0. High 5 retains more product-specific wording correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The announcer keeps the demonstration and public performance while reducing selected brief navigation and cue composition.
reach: Work with producers to connect commercial claims to the actual product evidence
skills_to_grow: Checking offer versions and claim qualifications
Measuring cue-writing work by its actual author
role.ambitious_version: Clear product demonstrations and accurate purchase information with human control of every public claim.

job.title: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
